title: Baldev Singh & Ors. v. State of Uttarakhand & Ors.
summary: Uttarakhand HC, Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia (20.08.2011), kai writ petitions ek saath. B.Ed. pass graduates ko, jinke graduation mein 50% (baad mein 45%) se kam the, primary teacher ke TET mein baithne nahi diya ja raha tha. Aadhaar tha NCTE ki 23.08.2010 ki notification aur State ka 29.04.2011 ka GO.
held: TET ki shart sahi hai, par graduation mein minimum % ki shart B.Ed. walon par unreasonable aur Article 14 ke khilaaf hai. Jinhone tab B.Ed. kiya jab 45% ki shart thi hi nahi (27.09.2007 se pehle), unki degree baad ki shart se "washed out" nahi ho sakti. Petitioners ko TET mein baithne diya jaaye.
use: Yeh Nainital HC ka apna faisla hai, aur baad mein Supreme Court ne Neeraj Kumar Rai (para 7) mein ise quote kiya.
Sateshwari jaisa hi tathya: graduation mein 45% se kam, aur B.Ed. 27.09.2007 se pehle (1999).
Faisla Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia ka hai, jo baad mein Supreme Court judge bane.
caution: Mudda TET mein baithne ki yogyata tha, niyukti ke baad seva samaapti nahi. Tark same hai, par tathya alag hain.
Primary (class I–V) ke liye B.Ed. ki chhoot NCTE ne 01.01.2012 tak hi di thi (page 27–28). Sateshwari ki niyukti kis level par hai, yeh dekhna zaroori hai.

quotes.text: The petitioners left before this Court are those petitioners, who have a B.Ed. degree from a recognized institute but they are graduates with less than 45 % in graduation. All these petitioners have done their B.Ed. when the 45% condition in graduation was not in force.

The only reasonable condition should be B.Ed. qualification, irrespective of one having any percentage of marks in his graduation. If one has done his B.Ed. from a recognized institute then this qualification cannot now be washed out.

…such a restriction (of having minimum percentage in graduation) is both unreasonable, unjust and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India. Therefore, this Court declares such condition of asking a minimum percentage of marks in graduation from those candidates who are B.Ed. qualified in NCTE notification dated 23.8.2010 and subsequent State Government Order dated 29.4.2011 as violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India.
